title: Lelouch vs Schneizel Analysed like Chess | Code Geass

moves.title: Freezing the world
moves.comment: Schneizel wants a world that never changes. Lelouch spots the problem: people do. A powerful plan is resting on a fragile assumption.

moves.title: Accepting death
moves.comment: Schneizel is ready to die. But he has decided what winning means for Lelouch without checking. That assumption is about to become expensive.

moves.title: Changing the win condition
moves.comment: Lelouch orders Schneizel to serve Zero. Killing him would waste a useful piece. Taking control wins the position and keeps the piece.

moves.title: Pre-recording the conversation
moves.comment: Schneizel was arguing with a recording. Lelouch predicted his answers and used the debate to conceal his approach. The conversation was the decoy.

moves.title: Recruiting the opponent
moves.comment: Schneizel shoots Diethard to protect Lelouch. The enemy piece has changed sides. Diethard notices the new team arrangement one move too late.
